clue.text: Arsenal's publication

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a store of ammunition or weapons
second meaning: a periodical such as a weekly glossy

explanation.surface: The football club Arsenal's own matchday programme or club journal.
explanation.walkthrough: Arsenal looks like the London football club, but here it is a plain noun: a store of weapons, which is also the sense of this word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a store for ammunition and a periodical issued regularly to readers.

clue.text: Matured by a good education

parts.note: taken as written
G is the standard abbreviation for good
Ed is short for education

explanation.surface: Someone who grew up thanks to fine schooling.
explanation.definitionFit: Wine or cheese that has matured has been left to grow older, so it is described with this adjective.

clue.text: Pain caused by a bit of sewing!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a sharp ache in the side after running
second meaning: one loop of thread made by a needle

explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation mark flags the play: the side-ache and the needlework loop share one word.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden sharp ache in the side while running shares its name with a single loop of thread in needlework.

clue.text: Inspire to live, concealing heart condition

indicators.note: a thing concealing another holds it hidden inside, so one piece wraps round the other

parts.note: to be is to exist or live

indicators.note: to condition something is to work it into a new state, so the word before it is rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A medical clue: giving life to someone who hides a cardiac complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heart condition' reads as a cardiac illness, but 'condition' works on the word heart. Inspire is used in its literal sense of drawing air in.
explanation.definitionFit: To inspire literally means to draw air into the lungs, which is exactly what this verb describes.

clue.text: Gush over animal

indicators.note: turned over means flipped round, so the word before is read backwards in this down entry

parts.note: to gush is to flow freely

explanation.surface: Someone gushing with enthusiasm about a creature.
explanation.definitionFit: A wild carnivore of the dog family, hunting in packs, is a typical example of an animal.

clue.text: Self-control and a bit of spine give rise to good ancestry

parts.note: a disc is one of the cushioning pieces of the spinal column

indicators.note: in a down entry something that rises is read upwards, so the word for good runs backwards

parts.note: pi, short for pious, is crosswordese for good
a line is a family's lineage

explanation.surface: Character and a strong back are said to come from good breeding.
explanation.walkthrough: PI for good comes from pious; written upwards it reads IP.
explanation.definitionFit: Discipline is the trained ability to restrain one's impulses, which is what self-control means.

clue.text: Child at home has cooler time

parts.note: someone at home is in
a fan is a device that cools you
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A youngster staying in has a more relaxed spell than others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cooler' reads as a comparative adjective, but it is a noun: something that cools.
explanation.definitionFit: A baby or very young child is an infant, the word for the earliest stage of childhood.

clue.text: Issue with changing of the guard

indicators.note: changing the letters of a phrase rearranges them, so these words signal a reshuffle

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A problem with the ceremonial Changing of the Guard at Buckingham Palace.
explanation.walkthrough: The Changing of the Guard is a London ceremony at Buckingham Palace. Issue here means offspring, not a problem.
explanation.definitionFit: Issue is a formal legal word for offspring, and a female child is one example of offspring.

clue.text: Working couple collect island vegetable

indicators.note: to collect something is to gather it in, so the pair holds the island letter between them

parts.note: working is on, and a couple means two of them
I is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: A two-income couple gather produce on an island farm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Working couple' looks like a pair of employed people, but it means the word for working, twice.
explanation.definitionFit: This pungent layered bulb is a common kitchen vegetable used in many savoury dishes.

clue.text: Poet changed heart of Mr Pitt

indicators.note: the middle letters are changed, meaning only the central pair is swapped while the ends stay put

parts.note: Brad Pitt is the Hollywood actor

explanation.surface: A poet reworked the core of a film star, or of the statesman William Pitt.
explanation.walkthrough: Mr Pitt suggests the British prime minister William Pitt, but it is the actor Brad Pitt.
explanation.definitionFit: A bard is an old or literary word for a poet; Shakespeare is known as the Bard.

clue.text: One extends journey to trade with Jamaica

parts.note: to traffic is to trade, often illicitly
JAM is the abbreviation for Jamaica

explanation.surface: A trader travels further to do business with Jamaica.
explanation.definitionFit: A queue of stationary vehicles on the road lengthens how long any trip takes, so it is something that extends a journey.

clue.text: Bit of fish on plate topped with garnish

indicators.note: something topped has had its top cut off, so the word loses its first letter

parts.note: a fin is part of a fish
a dish is a plate

explanation.surface: Plating up a piece of fish and adding a garnish on top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Garnish' looks like part of the cooking scene but is the definition, in the sense of a final decorative touch.
explanation.definitionFit: A garnish is a final decorative touch to a dish, and a finish is likewise a last surface treatment or adornment.

clue.text: Check naughty child's revision, including primarily music, English and numeracy

indicators.note: including means taking in, so the revision word holds the selected letters inside

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child
an edit is a revision of text

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter of each subject is used

parts.note: first letter
first letter
first letter

explanation.surface: Reviewing a mischievous pupil's exam preparation in the basics of music, English and maths.
explanation.walkthrough: Check is the noun for something that holds you back, not a verb meaning inspect.
explanation.definitionFit: A check is something that holds back progress, and an impediment is an obstacle or hindrance doing just that.

clue.text: Feel sorry for a VIP, they are suffering!

indicators.note: letters that are suffering have been knocked about, so they come out in a new order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Sympathy for a celebrity and their entourage who are having a hard time.
explanation.definitionFit: To show compassion or mercy toward someone in distress is the idiomatic phrase meaning to sympathise.

clue.text: Check on old soldier

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to examine carefully, as with a candidate
second meaning: short for veteran, chiefly American

explanation.surface: Looking in on an elderly ex-serviceman.
explanation.definitionFit: To vet is to screen or examine thoroughly, and in American usage a vet is a veteran of the armed forces.

clue.text: Bicycle's hollow wheel rod is custom-made

indicators.note: a hollow word has its insides emptied, leaving only the first and last letters

parts.note: outside letters only
a spoke is a rod joining hub to rim

explanation.surface: A hand-built bicycle with special hollow spokes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hollow wheel rod' reads as one tubular spoke, but 'hollow' acts on the word before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Bespoke describes goods such as suits made to a particular customer's order, the British word for tailor-made.

clue.text: Work I did to protect little one

indicators.note: the words protect something by wrapping round it, so the letters lie inside them

parts.note: found inside the run of letters across these words

explanation.surface: Someone describing the work they did to keep a child safe.
explanation.definitionFit: Kid is the informal word for a child, and a little one is an affectionate term for a small child.

clue.text: Bands are rubbish aboard ship

indicators.note: aboard means on a vessel, so the rubbish word goes inside the ship abbreviation

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
tripe is nonsense

explanation.surface: Musicians are dismissed as worthless for playing on a cruise ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bands' suggests groups of musicians, but it means strips of colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Stripes are long narrow strips of colour, and bands is a synonym in that pattern sense.

clue.text: Love Vermeer's work for all time

indicators.note: to work material is to knead it into a new shape, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like O
taken as written: the Dutch painter

explanation.surface: An art lover professing eternal devotion to Vermeer's paintings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vermeer's work' reads as the Dutch master's paintings, but 'work' acts on his name together with the love letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Evermore is a literary word meaning always or forever, which is what for all time means.

clue.text: I belong to rebel base

indicators.note: letters that rebel refuse to stay in line, so they fall into a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A recruit announcing they are part of an insurgents' camp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Base' looks like a rebel camp, but it is the adjective meaning low or dishonourable.
explanation.definitionFit: Base as an adjective means morally low and dishonourable, which is what ignoble means.

clue.text: Visual aid for leader on track?

definitions.text: Visual aid for leader on track?

parts.note: surface reading: a chart or slide used in a presentation, here for a race leader
setter's reading: an animal that leads a blind person along the path, helping them see the way

explanation.surface: A slide show or diagram prepared for whoever is out in front in a race.
explanation.walkthrough: A visual aid usually means a presentation chart; here it is an animal that aids sight, and it is the leader on the track.
explanation.definitionFit: A trained dog leads a blind owner along paths, acting as their eyes, so it is both a sight aid and a leader.

clue.text: Clamour for leading river rower

parts.note: a team that is up is ahead
R is the abbreviation for river
an oar is a person who rows

explanation.surface: Crowds shouting for the rower in front on the river.
explanation.walkthrough: An oar can be a rower as well as the blade, a common crossword sense.
explanation.definitionFit: An uproar is a loud noisy outcry, and clamour is a synonym for that din.

clue.text: Scholar abandoned tattered Baedeker that smelt awful

indicators.note: a tattered thing is torn up, so the remaining letters are scrambled
the scholar is abandoned, meaning those letters are left out of the guidebook name

parts.note: BA is a Bachelor of Arts
taken as written: a famous series of travel guidebooks

explanation.surface: An academic threw away a worn-out, foul-smelling old travel guide.
explanation.walkthrough: A Baedeker is a classic German travel guidebook. Removing BA leaves EDEKER to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: To reek is to give off a strong unpleasant odour, so the past tense means smelt awful.

clue.text: Live with desire for change …

indicators.note: a desire for change suggests reworking things, so the word is reordered

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Living with a longing for something different.
explanation.definitionFit: To reside somewhere is to dwell or make one's home there, the sense of live in a place.

clue.text: Three regular soldiers make America great

indicators.note: regular means at even intervals, so every other letter of the number is kept

parts.note: first, third and fifth letters
soldiers are men
to do is to make
US is the United States

explanation.surface: A dig at a political slogan: three regular troops will restore American greatness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regular soldiers' reads as professional troops, but 'regular' acts on the word three.
explanation.definitionFit: Tremendous means very large or excellent, and great is a synonym in both senses.

clue.text: … following web coverage of unknown

indicators.note: to give coverage of something is to cover it, so the web word wraps round the unknown letter

parts.note: a net is a web
X is the classic unknown quantity in algebra

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: internet reporting of an unknown story.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this to the previous clue for the surface only; the clue stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Next means coming immediately after in order, which is the sense of following.

clue.text: Notice retiring politician's a bit wet

indicators.note: retiring means withdrawing backwards, so the word for notice is read in reverse

parts.note: an ad is a notice
an MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: An observation that a politician about to step down is rather feeble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wet' is British slang for feeble, which suits a politician, but here it simply means moist.
explanation.definitionFit: Damp means slightly moist, so it describes something that is a little bit wet.

clue.text: Retirement place goes west with ton of money owed

indicators.note: going west on a map means moving right to left, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: you retire to bed at night
T is the abbreviation for ton

explanation.surface: A retirement home collapses with a huge sum in arrears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retirement place' suggests a care home, but retiring here is going to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A debt is a sum that one person is obliged to pay another, so it is money owed.

clue.text: Knights go in swinging axe and conquer

indicators.note: the knights go in, meaning they are placed inside the other letters
something swinging moves about wildly, so the weapon's letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
N is the chess abbreviation for knight; two for the plural

explanation.surface: Medieval knights charge in brandishing axes to seize territory.
explanation.definitionFit: To annex territory is to seize and take it over, which is what conquering a land does.

clue.text: Scottish landowner touring Germany returned by Beetle

indicators.note: touring means travelling round, so the landowner goes around the other letters

parts.note: a laird is a Scottish estate owner
D is the international vehicle code for Germany

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the small word next to it is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A Scottish laird on a German tour is sent home in a VW Beetle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beetle' with its capital looks like the Volkswagen car, but it is the insect. D for Germany is from car registration plates.
explanation.definitionFit: A ladybird is the British name for a small spotted red beetle, called a ladybug in America.
